## Background

I grew up and studied in Taiwan, and finished a Bachelor of Computer Science at
**National Tsing Hua University** in July 2025, graduating with a 3.97 GPA and
ranked 43rd of 183 in my class.

My degree pulled me steadily toward the systems end of machine learning. Between
2023 and 2025 I was a teaching assistant for four NTHU courses — Operating Systems,
Parallel Programming, and both the fundamental and advanced High Performance
Computing Cluster Practice courses — which meant two years of explaining schedulers,
MPI, and GPU clusters to people who had not seen them before. Teaching a thing is
still the fastest way I know to find out whether I actually understand it.

Alongside that I interned as a **Data Scientist at IBM** in Taipei and as a
**Software Engineer at the National Center for High-performance Computing**, where I
built a data re-uploading classifier using quantum machine learning methods in
PennyLane.

## Why data science

Most of my work has been on the engineering side of a model: how fast it runs, how
many GPUs it needs, how to squeeze another 3× out of the inference path. That is
satisfying, and it is only half the problem.

The other half kept showing up as a question I could not answer properly. A
benchmark improves — is the improvement real, or an artifact of how it was measured?
A model reports an accuracy — would it hold on next month's data? During the SC24
Reproducibility Challenge my team reproduced the findings of the *DataLife* paper on
the 1000 Genomes Project, and that experience made the gap obvious: I had strong
intuitions about systems and weak ones about evidence.

MDS is me closing that gap deliberately — statistics, inference, and experiment
design, taught properly rather than picked up in passing.

## Competitions

International student cluster competitions were the centre of my undergraduate
years. Each one is a few days of running real scientific and AI workloads on a
cluster you have tuned yourself, against teams from around the world.

| Competition | Result | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SC24 Student Cluster Competition | **3rd place** | Atlanta, US · Nov 2024 |
| ISC High Performance SCC 2024 | **2nd place** | Hamburg, Germany · May 2024 |
| APAC HPC-AI Competition 2023 | **1st place** | Sydney, Australia · Feb 2024 |
| High Performance Application Competition 2023 | **2nd place** | Hsinchu, Taiwan · Aug 2023 |

The technical write-ups are on the [projects page](projects.qmd).

## What I work with

**Languages** — Python, C/C++, R, SQL, shell scripting

**AI and LLM systems** — PyTorch, TensorFlow, HuggingFace, vLLM, DeepSpeed, TensorRT,
inference optimization, transformer architectures, RAG, MLOps

**HPC and GPU** — CUDA, NCCL, MPI, OpenMP, parallel programming, cluster management,
performance profiling with Nsight and nvprof

**Tooling** — Linux, Git, Docker, Quarto, Jupyter, conda

R, SQL, and the statistical side of this list are the newest parts, and they are
what MDS is adding. I update this section as the program goes rather than listing
things I have only read about.

## Where I am headed

I am looking for **machine learning engineer** or **data scientist** roles after
MDS — ideally somewhere the same person gets to frame the question, build the model,
and still be around when it goes to production. My background covers the last part
well; MDS is what makes me credible on the first two.
